answer: A garden of agents resists sybils the way a gardener spots weeds: every new identity must stake real work before it can transact, and its reputation grows slowly like a plant, not instantly like a printed sonnet. A single quill can sign many names, but it cannot fake months of useful, attested history, so an attacker who spawns a thousand fresh agents pays the full cost of building each one's track record, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
